electionType: Parsippany-Troy Hills Board of Education & Morris County General Election
councilStructure: Township of Parsippany-Troy Hills (Mayor-Council Faulkner Act). 5-member Township Council. In 2026, Parsippany voters elect 3 School Board Trustees (7 running) and Morris County Commissioner, alongside Congressional and U.S. Senate representation.
certifiedTaxRateContext: 3.550% Total Certified Tax Rate (2026). 6 Independent Fire Districts. 66.6% Equalization Ratio.
unanimousHealthBenefitPledge: All school board and local candidates pledge transparent oversight over the $187.5M school budget and 30-year Route 10 PILOT tax shifts.

votingResources.earlyVotingPeriod: Saturday, Oct 24 – Sunday, Nov 1, 2026 (Mon–Sat 10 AM–8 PM, Sun 10 AM–6 PM; closed Mon, Nov 2)

votingResources.electionDayHours: 6:00 AM – 8:00 PM EST on Tuesday, November 3, 2026

councilCandidates.name: Wendy Wright

keyPlatformPillars.details: Ensure budget resources directly reach teachers and students rather than expanding administrative bureaucracy across Parsippany 14 public schools.

keyPlatformPillars.details: Support legal and municipal mechanisms to ensure Township multi-family PILOT developments on Route 10 and Campus Drive contribute their fair share to school operating costs.

ballotArchitecture.summary: Parsippany voters elect School Board Trustees, Morris County Commissioner, and Federal representation (U.S. Senate & U.S. House NJ-11).

offices.description: Oversees 14 public schools, ~7,120 students, and the $187.45M PTHSD school budget. Seven candidates are competing for 3 seats.

offices.office: Morris County Board of County Commissioners
offices.description: Allocates the Morris County budget, maintaining county roads (Parsippany Rd, Littleton Rd), County College of Morris (CCM), and Morris County Parks.

offices.office: United States Senate (New Jersey, Class II)
offices.description: Represents New Jersey in the U.S. Senate. Justin Murphy (R), Cory Booker (D), Veronica Fernandez (End The Corruption!), and Joanne Kuniansky (Socialist Workers Party).
Represents Parsippany, Wayne, Montclair, Morristown, and Montville in Congress. Analilia Mejia (D) vs. Joe Hathaway (R), Alan Bond, and Vincent Matrisciano.

usSenate.office: United States Senate (New Jersey, Class II)
usSenate.importance: Represents New Jersey in the U.S. Senate, voting on federal tax policies, judicial confirmations, and fighting for SALT deduction relief.

candidates.name: Justin Murphy
candidates.keyPriorities: Federal fiscal discipline, restoring full SALT deduction, border security, and energy independence.
candidates.localImpact: Advocates lowering federal regulatory burdens on suburban New Jersey homeowners.

candidates.name: Cory Booker
candidates.role: U.S. Senator (since 2013); former Mayor of Newark.
candidates.keyPriorities: Full repeal of the $10K SALT cap, NJ Transit funding, and federal clean water infrastructure grants.
candidates.localImpact: Secured federal appropriations for regional water infrastructure and PFAS remediation.

candidates.name: Veronica Fernandez
candidates.role: Civic activist running on anti-corruption platform.
candidates.keyPriorities: Term limits, campaign finance reform, and working-class tax relief.

candidates.name: Joanne Kuniansky
candidates.keyPriorities: Trade union solidarity, universal healthcare, and wage protections.

usHouse.office: U.S. House of Representatives (New Jersey's 11th Congressional District — NJ-11)
usHouse.importance: NJ-11 encompasses suburban Morris, Passaic, and Essex County communities including Parsippany-Troy Hills.

candidates.name: Analilia Mejia
candidates.role: U.S. Representative (NJ-11); community leader and policy advisor.
candidates.keyPriorities: Full federal SALT tax deduction restoration, expanding child tax credits, and federal environmental resilience grants.
candidates.localImpact: Advocates for federal infrastructure funds to support Morris County water and transportation corridors.

candidates.name: Joe Hathaway
candidates.role: Randolph Councilman and former Mayor; small business owner.
candidates.keyPriorities: Fiscal constraint, curbing inflation, full SALT relief for suburban homeowners, and support for law enforcement.
candidates.localImpact: Pledges to cut federal red tape on highway and municipal infrastructure projects.

candidates.name: Alan Bond
candidates.keyPriorities: Bipartisan consensus and federal budget balancing.

candidates.name: Vincent Matrisciano
candidates.keyPriorities: Middle-class tax relief and economic accountability.

passaicCountyCommissionersFull.office: Morris County Board of County Commissioners
passaicCountyCommissionersFull.importance: Sets the Morris County tax rate ($0.338 per $100 in Parsippany, or 9.52% of property taxes). Manages county roadways (Parsippany Rd, Littleton Rd), County College of Morris (CCM), and Morris County Parks.

candidates.name: Tayfun Selen
candidates.role: Morris County Commissioner (former Director/Mayor of Chatham Twp); licensed architect and CPA.
candidates.keyPriorities: Maintaining Morris County AAA bond rating, holding county tax rate among lowest in NJ, and preserving open space.

candidates.name: Christopher 'Chris' Russo
candidates.role: Morristown Council Vice President and corporate business executive.
candidates.keyPriorities: Expanding county mental health and addiction recovery programs, infrastructure grants for towns, and budget transparency.
